purpose: The feature walkthrough band of a product page: a horizontal section title, with its button beside the headline, over up to three tabs on one side and the active tab's media on the other. A tab's media is its own code file (a `code-block` with line numbers whose lines rise in while the tab is open, on a pixelate texture in a taller stage), the band's live scene (handed the open tab's `value`), or the tab's illustration. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-tabs-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `registration-frame`, `media-tabs`, `code-block`, `illustration`, `button`, `link` and the webkit scene assets. The tabs advance on a timer that pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus and never runs under reduced motion; that state is owned by `media-tabs`.
useWhen: Use FeatureTabsSection for up to three tabs beside a media on a product page.
To walk through the two or three features behind one claim, one picture at a time, like Functions' Observability.
avoidWhen: For architectures drawn as diagrams across the full width → use `architecture-tabs-section`.
For a scroll-driven walkthrough of more features → use `feature-scroll-section`.
related: `media-tabs` — the timed tabs this section renders through.
`illustration` — the picture a tab shows when it has no code and the band has no scene.
`code-block` — the code file a tab opens as its media.
bestPractices: Keep to three tabs; tabs past the limit are not rendered.
Give every tab an `illustrationLabel` saying what its picture shows.
Use tab `code` when the feature is an API a developer reads; keep each file short enough to read in the stage. Set `copyAriaLabel` to say what the copy button copies.

Use the band `scene` when one console widget plays a different beat per tab (`{ component: 'ConsoleMockup', props: { name: 'functions-start' } }` with tab `value`s naming its tabs); give every tab a `value` then.
